messages.content: is we was at home a correct sentence?
use we were at home. with we, were is the correct word for that sentence.
what if i am talking only about myself?
then say i was at home. i was is about one person, while we were is about that person and other people together.
explain simply.
i was is about you. we were is about you and another person or more people together.
give two short examples.
i was at home alone. we were at home together.
can you make a small story with both?
i was at home alone in the morning. after lunch, my sister came back. we were at home together for the afternoon.
does using we give you the number of people there?
no. we puts the person talking in a group, but does not always give a number.
answer simply.
no. you need more detail to know the number of people.
which is better, did you go or did you went?
did you go is correct. did already makes the question about the past, so use go after it.
what does the answer use?
you can answer i went. for example: did you go to the park? yes, i went after lunch.
make it about not going.
did you go to the park? no, i did not go. i stayed home.
why is went not in that no answer?
with did not, use go, just as you use go after did in the question. i went is a past answer, while i did not go says it did not happen.
explain simply.
you can say i went for yes. with did not, say i did not go.
write a short conversation where i ask if my brother went with someone.
did you go to the park alone? no, i went with our cousin. did you stay long? we stayed until after lunch, then came home.
does alone mean only one person is in the park?
no. it can mean the person did not go with someone. other people may still be in the park.
answer simply.
no. someone can go alone and still see other people there.
i want to clean the table before starting a letter. i finished moving the books, but the table still needs washing. can i say the cleaning is done?
not if washing is still part of the task. you finished one part, moving the books, but the whole cleaning task still has work left.
what can i write in a note without making it sound like i did nothing?
books put away. table still needs washing before writing the letter.
can you make that a full sentence?
i put the books away, but i still need to wash the table before writing my letter.
does but take away the first fact?
no. it keeps both facts: some work is done, and some is left. you do not need to choose between saying everything is finished and saying nothing is finished.
now i wash the table. write the new note.
the table is clean and ready for writing. the books are already put away.
why not keep still needs washing?
you gave new information that the washing is done. the note should use what happened, rather than keep saying washing is left to do.
answer simply.
you washed it, so the note should no longer say that washing is left to do.
write a simple conversation where i ask whether a restaurant has soup today, rather than saying i know it does.
do you have soup today? yes, we do. could i have some, please? would you like bread with it? yes, thank you.
now change the answer so there is no soup.
do you have soup today? not today, i am sorry. what food do you have? we have rice and vegetables. then i would like that, please.
does no soup today mean the restaurant never has soup?
no. the answer is about today. it does not tell us what they have on every other day.
say it simply.
no. the answer is about today. another day can be different.
what should i ask if i want to know about tomorrow?
will you have soup tomorrow?
can the worker answer i do not know yet?
yes. that is a clear answer when the food plan for tomorrow is not known. it is better than giving a sure answer without the information.
what can i say back?
thank you. i will ask again tomorrow.
i left a small container at a hotel, but i do not know which room it is in now. help me ask whether someone found it.
i think i left a small container at the hotel. has anyone found it?
i know i left it there. do not say i think.
i left a small container at the hotel. has anyone found it?
can you ask where i should come to get it if it was found?
i left a small container at the hotel. has anyone found it? if so, where should i come to get it?
what if i only know it was in my room before i left?
then add that detail without choosing its place now: it was in my room before i left, but i do not know where it is now.
should you say a worker moved it?
not unless that is information you have. someone may have moved it, but you have not said that happened.
write one short message with only the things i know.
i left a small container in my hotel room before leaving. has anyone found it, and where should i come to get it?
does asking where it is say it has been found already?
not in that message. has anyone found it keeps that part as a question before asking what to do if the answer is yes.
write a story about a nurse and a teacher meeting in a garden after work. keep it about their time together and the garden, rather than their work.

a nurse and a teacher meet near a garden table after work. the nurse brings a cup of tea, and the teacher brings a picture a child drew. they look at the picture and then at the real tree in front of them. the child made the tree blue, and they ask each other what idea the child had. they choose not to make the whole conversation about work. instead, they talk about what they want to grow in the garden and how the evening feels.
make it simple.
a nurse and a teacher meet in a garden after work. they look at a picture made by a child, then talk about the real tree and what they want to grow near it.
child picture needs better grammar.
they look at a picture made by a child, then talk about the real tree and what they want to grow near it.
does being a nurse mean every conversation has to be about health?
no. a person can have work and still talk about other parts of life. the story asked for time together in a garden.
what can the teacher ask about the garden?
what would you like to grow here next?
end with them choosing to ask the group before changing the garden they use together.
they plan to ask the people in the garden group before choosing what to plant.
say it simply.
they will ask the group before choosing a new plant for the garden.
can we say we worked it out ourselves if we used a note with a rule on it?
you can do the thinking as a group while using a written rule. if you want it clear, say you used the note but chose the answer together.
answer simply.
you used a rule, but still did the thinking together. you can say that clearly rather than say no help was used at all.
use ourselves in a sentence.
we used the rule on the note and worked out the answer ourselves.
does that sentence say nobody helped write the rule before?
no. it says what your group did with the rule. it does not tell us who wrote it or what help they had.
write a small example with two people reading a game rule.
two people read a rule saying to move one object at a time. they look at the objects and choose their next move together. they used the written rule, but worked out the move themselves.
what if someone else told them the answer?
then saying ourselves without saying how the other person helped may give the wrong idea. keep that help in the story.
say it simply.
if someone gave the answer, they should keep that help in the story rather than say they chose it all themselves.
my uncle says he may visit next week. can i tell my sister he is coming for sure?
no. may keeps the visit possible rather than sure. you can say he may come, but should not change that to a sure visit without more information.
say my question simply.
my uncle says he may visit next week. can i say he will come for sure?
what if he later says he bought a train ticket?
that is more detail about his plan, but you can still ask whether the visit is now chosen for sure. do not turn one new detail into every answer about the visit.
write that question.
does having the ticket mean you have chosen to visit next week?
he says yes, and he will come after lunch. write a short message to my sister.
our uncle has chosen to visit next week. he says he will come after lunch.
does that give a day of the week?
no. next week is still general. you may need to ask which day before making a plan to meet him.
what can i ask him next?
which day next week will you come?
i met someone at school and learned their name. does that mean i know them well now?
not just from a name. you know one useful detail, but learning about a person takes more conversation and time than that.
can you give me one simple question for talking again?
what do you like doing after school?
what if they only say reading?
you can ask one follow up about that: what kind of story do you enjoy? keep it as a conversation rather than asking many questions without listening.
if they say they like every book, should i test them with ten different books?
not unless they want that kind of game. in a simple conversation, every book may just mean they enjoy reading very much. you can ask for one example they liked instead.
say it simply.
they may mean they enjoy reading very much. ask for one example they liked, rather than turning the reply into a test.
write that question.
what is one book you enjoyed?
can i still not know everything about them after the answer?
yes. each answer gives part of a person life, rather than every fact about them.
fix person life with the words we have.
each answer gives part of what a person wants to share, rather than every fact about them.
i drew a circle, then a square next to it. can i say i drew the same shape again?
no. a circle and a square do not have the same shape. you drew another shape on the same page, rather than the same shape again.
answer simply.
no. the circle is one shape, and the square is a different one. the page is the same, but the shape is not.
now i draw another circle. which one is the same kind of shape as the first?
the new circle is the same kind of shape as the first circle. it is still another drawing, not the very same object on the page.
why is same kind not the same as same object?
one circle can be on the left and another on the right. both have the same kind of shape, but they are two things you drew.
explain simply.
same kind can be about two things. same object is about one thing being the very same one.
write a question that asks how many things are on the page, rather than how many are of one kind.
how many things did you draw on the page?
now answer with the facts i gave.
you drew three things: a circle, a square, and another circle.
write a story about a sister leaving food for her brother with a note. the note should say what is there without saying she knows how hungry he will be.

a woman cooks rice and vegetables before going out. her brother will come home later, so she keeps some food for him. she writes where it is, but not that it will be enough, because she does not know how hungry he will be. when he comes home, he reads the note, finds the food, and sends a thank you message before sitting down.
make it simple.
a woman cooks rice and vegetables and keeps some for her brother. she leaves a note saying where it is. he comes home, reads the note, and thanks her before eating.
write the note itself using kitchen as the place.
i left rice and vegetables in the kitchen for you. i kept some before going out.
can you write that without using there is or there are?
yes. i left rice and vegetables in the kitchen for you makes the food and place clear.
give only the better note.
i left rice and vegetables in the kitchen for you.
did i tell you what feeling she wanted to add to the note?
no. the note only needs the food and place from the story. you did not give another feeling to add.
write only the facts.
i left rice and vegetables in the kitchen for you.
picoboi, change yesterday to tomorrow in i returned the book yesterday.
i will return the book tomorrow.
why did returned change too?
tomorrow is about a later time, so i changed returned to will return. keeping i returned the book tomorrow would not give the same clear grammar.
explain simply.
yesterday goes with returned in the first sentence. tomorrow goes with will return in the new plan.
does changing the writing mean i really still have the book?
no. it is a writing example. the change does not tell me what happened with your real book.
answer simply.
no. changing a sentence for an example does not give a new fact about the real book.
now make a question about my friend returning it.
will you return the book tomorrow?
did that keep me as the person returning it?
no. changing i to you made your friend the person being asked. if you want to ask about yourself, use: will i return the book tomorrow?
write a question asking whether i can return it tomorrow, rather than saying i will.
can i return the book tomorrow?
say my request simply.
ask whether returning the book tomorrow is okay.
